_comment: Price table for api/jd-rate.php (the reveal payload) and scripts/jd-spend.php.
All figures are USD per MILLION tokens.
Keys are jd_generations.model_version — the exact provider wire string that
jd-generate.php sent (the pool's api_model), so a model swap in
api/jd-config.php only needs a matching key added here.
Field meanings, normalised across all four providers by api/jd-usage.php:
input       uncached input tokens
output      output tokens (for OpenAI this INCLUDES reasoning tokens,
because completion_tokens already counts them; for Google it
INCLUDES thoughtsTokenCount, billed as output)
cache_write Anthropic 5-minute cache writes; 0 for the others (OpenAI and
Moonshot have no such charge; Google implicit caching likewise)
cache_read  Anthropic cache hits / OpenAI cached input tokens / Moonshot
automatic-cache hits / Google cachedContentTokenCount
VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING A LARGE NUMBER: providers change prices. Re-check the
source URLs below and update _fetched when you do.
_fetched 2026-10-02 (the pool refresh, taxonomy poolVersion pool-2026-10-02)
covers the four POOL rows only: claude-opus-5-5, gpt-6-astra, kimi-k3 and
gemini-3.1-pro-preview, each checked against its vendor's own page (_notes).
The other rows were not re-checked and keep their earlier sourcing.

_notes.claude-opus-5-5: Pool member from 2026-10-02. Confirmed 2026-10-02 on https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing: $4 base input / $5 5-minute cache write / $0.20 cache hit (0.05x input on this model, not the usual 0.1x) / $20 output per million (1-hour cache write $8, never used here: the drawer sends no cache_control). Agrees with the bundled Claude API reference's model table.
_notes.gpt-6-astra: Pool member from 2026-10-02. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra (fetched 2026-10-02): $10 input / $1 cached input / $50 output per million; prompts over 272K tokens bill 2x input and cached input and 1.5x output (our prompts are tiny, so the base tier is the one that applies). No cache-write charge.
_notes.claude-sonnet-5-5: Added 2026-10-02 for the intake clerk (taxonomy.json utility.intake, api/jd2-intake.php) from the bundled Claude API reference's model table: $2 in / $10 out per million, cache reads $0.20 (same prices as Sonnet 5). cache_write 2.50 is the standard 1.25x-input 5-minute write rate, not separately sourced (intake sends no cache_control, so it is never charged). _fetched is NOT bumped: the other rows were not re-checked.
_notes.claude-sonnet-5: Introductory $2/$10 runs through 2026-08-31; standard $3/$15 starts 2026-09-01. Update this entry if you switch the pair to Sonnet 5 after that date.
_notes.gpt-5.4: Prices shown are the <272K context tier.
_notes.gpt-5.5: Prices shown are the <272K context tier.
_notes.kimi-k3: Confirmed 2026-10-02 on https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat: $3.00 input / $0.30 cached input / $15.00 output per million, 1,048,576-token context. Moonshot's automatic context caching has no write charge; hits bill at the cache_read rate. The page also lists explicit cache-write prices ($3.00 for a 5-minute TTL, $6.00 for 1 hour); the drawer never creates an explicit cache, so cache_write stays 0. Still the flagship on https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/models (no dated snapshot, nothing newer listed).
_notes.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Confirmed 2026-10-02 on Google's own page, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (paid tier, prompts <= 200K tokens): $2.00 input / $12.00 output including thinking tokens / $0.20 context caching per million (> 200K: $4 / $18 / $0.40; caching storage $4.50 per million tokens per hour, never incurred here). That settles the two old doubts: the earlier aggregator's $1/$6 claim for the preview id does not match the vendor page, and the 0.20 cache_read is now sourced rather than estimated. Still the newest Pro-line model on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models.
_notes.gpt-6.1-sol: Pool member from 2026-10-02 (replaces gpt-6-astra as the OpenAI chair, owner call). https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models lists GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 input / $10 output per million, 1.05M context, 128K max output; the page shows no cached-input rate for it, so cache_read 0.20 is INFERRED at Astra's 10% ratio — correct it when the model page states one.
